title: Heat-engine efficiency
target: Calculate useful output and rejected energy for a heat engine.
criteria: Distinguish an ideal upper bound from actual performance.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A cyclic engine takes 600 J of heat and delivers 180 J of work. What is efficiency?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A modeled engine has 25% efficiency and receives 800 J per cycle. What work output follows?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A cyclic heat engine receives 450 J and does 120 J of work. How much heat is rejected?
cpa.guide: With no net energy storage over a cycle, Q_out = Q_in − W = 330 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An engine takes in 900 J and rejects 630 J each cycle. What is useful work?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An ideal model places an upper efficiency bound of 40% on an engine’s operating temperatures. Which actual performance is consistent with that bound?
cpa.guide: A real device may operate below an ideal upper bound; values above it are inconsistent with those assumptions.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A team reports 55% measured efficiency where the stated ideal maximum is 45%. What should be checked?
options: The ideal bound guarantees every real engine is exactly 45%.
The claim should be accepted solely because it is measured.
Measurements, energy accounting, temperatures, and assumptions.
cpa.guide: Exceeding the stated bound calls for checking data and model applicability, not accepting a perpetual gain.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
